00:00 Lena: Hi everyone, thanks for joining the QBR, I'm Lena from Redwood, I'll kick us off. We've got Marco from the SE team as well. Quick roll call?
00:10 Aisha: Hey all, Aisha here - head of MLOps at Veritas. Tom's on and Priya will chime in for ops.
00:16 Tom: Hey, Tom Reed, CTO.
00:18 Priya: Priya, SRE lead, hi.
00:20 Lena: Great. High level agenda - usage, costs, reliability, then roadmaps and next steps. Marco, do you want to take the usage slide?
00:30 Marco: Yeah, sure. So from Redwood side we've been watching your token volumes - monthly avg is up about 38% quarter over quarter, driven by the new semantic search route and increased chat sessions. Most of the spike is from the prod-search indexer and some bursty weekend loads.
00:46 Aisha: Yup that matches our internal metrics. Question on the billing - the invoice seems higher than we expected, is that mainly model choice or the embedding jobs?
00:54 Lena: Great question. Short answer: a combination. The embedding jobs are heavy, and the chat endpoints are using the larger model family for higher fidelity. We'll put together a per-route, per-model breakdown.
01:06 Marco: Also worth noting you have a fair amount of re-run/pipeline retries which double counts tokens sometimes - we flagged a couple of ETL tasks calling the chat route.
01:15 Aisha: Oh oof, ok we'll look into that.
01:18 Tom: On reliability, we had a small outage mid-November, ~35 minutes of elevated latency. Do you have the root cause from your side?
01:25 Marco: Yes - that was a region failover where the autoscaler overwhelmed a pod group and we hit a transient NVMe saturation in the Dedicated host pool - or sorry, I mean in the host farm used by the Dedicated customer instances - the logs show queueing in the runtime. There's an automated fallback but it was slower than expected.
01:45 Priya: Can you clarify - we thought we were on Hosted not Dedicated?
01:48 Lena: You're right, Veritas is on Hosted but with a soft reservation burst profile. The incident was in the same cloud region that impacted multiple tenants; our routing policy failed over to a colder variant which added latency.
02:00 Tom: So would Dedicated have prevented that?
02:03 Marco: Dedicated would give you isolated GPU pools and an SLA-backed throughput. It wouldn't be 100% magic - if your job spikes beyond committed capacity, you still need burst handling. But overall isolates noisy neighbors and gives predictable latency.
02:18 Aisha: We're trying to weigh the cost delta. Dedicated pricing looks pretty big on paper.
02:22 Lena: Totally. That's why we'll run an ROI estimate - balancing token-unit cost and the improvement in tail latency. Also consider quantization or smaller model variants for non-latency critical routes - that can lower per-token cost significantly.
02:36 Tom: We're also interested in Private (VPC) options. Data residency and KMS integration are musts for us.
02:41 Marco: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS/HSM integration. We can share the network diagram and the SOC2 artifacts. There are some tradeoffs - on-prem may need different kernel selections and can affect throughput.
02:55 Priya: For compliance, we need audit logs retention for 12 months and SSO via SAML. How does Redwood handle RBAC and audit trails?
03:03 Lena: We support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC. Audit logs include request-level metadata and are exportable to your SIEM; retention is configurable as an add-on. We'll include the SOC2 Type II and sample audit log schema in the follow-up.
03:20 Aisha: Thank you. On the performance front, we saw higher p95 during business hours on search. Any tuning suggestions?
03:27 Marco: Two levers - smarter batching and prefix/KV cache. For search, prefix caching across similar queries reduces KV cache misses. Also, toggling continuous batching parameters can lower p95 without inflating cold-start latency. We'll propose concrete batch size and latency SLO tradeoffs.
03:45 Tom: Do we need to change inference model or just config?
03:48 Marco: Likely config first - batching and cache. If you need lower latency, smaller quantized variants or distillation can help, but that's a quality tradeoff.
03:57 Aisha: About the November incident - do you have a postmortem link?
04:01 Lena: Yes, short PM attached in the notes. It describes the failover path and mitigation. We also added a fallback model variant to reduce impact in similar scenarios.
04:10 Priya: Can Redwood run our synthetic workload to validate the Dedicated sizing?
04:14 Marco: Absolutely. We can schedule a 1k request run with your production prompts and provide latency and GPU util traces. That'll help size committed vGPU counts and autoscale policy.
04:25 Tom: Timeline wise - procurement wants an estimate by end of month. Can you commit to providing numbers by Dec 20?
04:30 Lena: Yes, we'll aim for Dec 20 for the sizing and cost estimate.
04:33 Aisha: On the roadmap, we're planning new features for fine-grained personalization requiring encrypted context storage - any notes on KMS integration?
04:40 Marco: The Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK (bring your own key). We'll detail the key rotation and key access policies.
04:52 Tom: Any blockers you see from Redwood's side for a VPC deployment in Q1?
04:56 Lena: Nothing major - network peering and procurement lead times are typical. We'll send a runbook for the VPC onboarding and estimated lead times.
05:05 Priya: Do you expose metrics to our Prometheus stack?
05:08 Marco: Yes, we have a metrics export and tracing hooks - we can push to your Prometheus/Grafana with a secure endpoint.
05:14 Aisha: Cost optimization - any quick wins we can implement immediately?
05:18 Marco: Yes: 1) Move non-critical batch jobs to a quantized model, 2) Deduplicate retry logic in your ETL to cut replays, 3) Enable prefix caching for search, 4) Consider request-level sampling for low-value routes.
05:31 Tom: Sounds good. Let's talk about the legal side briefly - data residency and DPA changes required?
05:36 Lena: Our standard DPA covers EU data residency; for bespoke terms we'll loop in legal. We'll attach the standard DPA and a summary of differences for Private deployments.
05:46 Aisha: Anything else on the roadmap alignment?
05:48 Marco: We saw your note asking for roadmap support for 'incremental reranking' - we can prioritize an eval for reranker quantization and share a benchmark spreadsheet.
05:59 Tom: Good. Can you send the benchmark template?
06:02 Lena: Yep, will include.
06:04 [silence / typing]
06:10 Lena: Okay, let's do a quick recap of action items. Marco?
06:13 Marco: I'll run the perf test and share results by Dec 20; I'll also draft recommended batching/cache settings.
06:20 Lena: I'll send the detailed cost breakdown and current invoices by Dec 17 and attach SOC2 and network diagram by Dec 18.
06:27 Priya: I'll send over compliance questions and retention requirements by Dec 18.
06:32 Tom: I'll confirm procurement timeline and approvers by Dec 22.
06:35 Aisha: Great. Any final questions?
06:38 Priya: One thing - can we get a short session on KV cache internals? Our infra engs want deeper details.
06:44 Marco: Yes, we can do a technical deep-dive next week; I'll propose times in the follow-up.
06:49 Lena: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and calendar invites.
06:52 Tom: Thanks, appreciate it.
06:54 Aisha: Thanks all.
07:00 [meeting ends]
